## Why This Is Asked
Probes ability to design CKNE-aware streaming with tail-latency SLO, multi-tenant fairness, and dynamic scaling.

## Key Concepts
- CKNE-to-concurrency mapping and bounds
- Dynamic backpressure and per-tenant queues
- Partition/operator rebalance and windowing strategies
- SLA guarantees and starvation avoidance

## Code Example
```
// Pseudo scheduling loop
for every 60s:
  for each tenant:
    ckne = getCKNE(tenant)
    desiredPar = clamp(basePar * (1 + k * ckne), minPar, maxPar)
    adjustPartitions(tenant, desiredPar)
    if ckne high: addInstance(tenant)
    if ckne low: dropInstance(tenant)
```

- How would you ensure no starvation for low-CKNE tenants during sustained high load?

## Why This Is Asked

- CKNE to per-tenant processing priority
- Token-bucket or quota-based throttling

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo: simple per-tenant rate limiter template
class TokenBucket {
  constructor(rate, capacity){ this.rate=rate; this.capacity=capacity; this.tokens=capacity; this.last=Date.now(); }
  tryConsume(n=1){ const now=Date.now(); const elapsed=(now-this.last)/1000; this.tokens = Math.min(this.capacity, this.tokens + elapsed*this.rate); this.last=now; if(this.tokens>=n){ this.tokens-=n; return true; } return false; }
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
In production, telemetry budgets must adapt to tenant criticality. A CKNE-driven tracer lets you protect high-value tenants during spikes without blowing out storage.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant CKNE-based resource control
- Adaptive sampling budgets
- Telemetry budget enforcement
- Testing methodology

## Code Example

```javascript
function samplingFromCKNE(ckne, max=1.0){
  // map 0-1 CKNE to 0-100% sampling
  return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, ckne)) * max;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate this approach in canary deployments?
- How would you handle CKNE drift or abrupt traffic pattern changes?
